title: Ionic Bonding Examples
page_title: Ionic Bonding Examples | Cambridge (CIE) A Level Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- Sodium is a Group 1 **metal**

  - It **loses** its outer electron to form a sodium ion with a +1 charge (Na<sup>+</sup>)
- Chlorine is a Group 7 **non-metal**

  - It **gains** 1 electron to form a chloride ion with a -1 charge (Cl<sup>-</sup>)
- The oppositely charged ions are attracted to each other by **electrostatic forces** to form NaCl (ionic bonds)
- The final ionic solid is **neutral** in charge

blocks.text: Dot and cross diagram to show the ionic bonding in sodium chloride

blocks.alt: Diagram showing sodium atom losing an electron to chlorine, forming a positive sodium ion and a negative chloride ion, illustrating cation and anion.
blocks.caption: Sodium gives its one outer electron to chlorine forming the ionic compound, sodium chloride

blocks.md:
- Magnesium is a Group 2 **metal**

  - It **loses** its 2 outer electrons to form a magnesium ion with a +2 charge (Mg<sup>2+</sup>)
- Oxygen is a Group 6 **non-metal**

  - It **gains** 2 electrons to form an oxide ion with a -2 charge (O<sup>2-</sup>)
- The oppositely charged ions are attracted to each other to by **electrostatic forces **to form MgO (ionic bonds)
- The final ionic solid is **neutral** in charge

blocks.text: Dot and cross diagram to show the ionic bonding in magnesium oxide

blocks.alt: Diagram showing magnesium atom losing 2 electrons to become a cation; oxygen atom gains these electrons to become a negatively charged anion.
blocks.caption: Magnesium gives both outer electrons to oxygen forming the ionic compound, magnesium oxide

blocks.md:
- Calcium is a Group 2 **metal**

  - It **loses** its 2 outer electrons to form a calcium ion with a +2 charge (Ca<sup>2+</sup>)
- Fluorine is a Group 7 **non-metal**

  - It **gains** 1 electron to form a fluoride ion with a -1 charge (F<sup>-</sup>)
- As before, the positive and negative ions are attracted to each other via an ionic bond
- However, to cancel out the 2+ charge of the calcium ion, 2 fluorine atoms are needed

  - Each fluorine atom can only accept 1 electron from the calcium atom
  - 2 fluoride ions will be formed
- Calcium fluoride is made when 1 calcium ion and 2 fluoride ions form ionic bonds, CaF<sub>2</sub>
- The final ionic solid of CaF<sub>2</sub> is **neutral** in charge

blocks.text: Dot and cross diagram to show the ionic bonding in calcium fluoride

blocks.alt: Diagram illustrating calcium atom donating electrons to fluorine atoms, forming a calcium cation and two fluoride anions through ionic bonding.
blocks.caption: Calcium gives away both outer electrons. Each fluorine receives one of those electrons forming the ionic compound, calcium fluoride

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
**Dot & cross lithium nitride**

Draw a dot and cross diagram for lithium nitride, Li<sub>3</sub>N.

**Answer**

- Lithium is a Group 1 **metal**

  - It **loses** its outer electron to form a lithium ion with a +1 charge (Li<sup>+</sup>)
- Nitrogen is a Group 5 **non-metal**

  - It **gains** 3 electrons to form a nitride ion with a -3 charge (N<sup>3-</sup>)
- To cancel out the -3 charge of the nitride ion, 3 lithium atoms are needed and 3 lithium ions will be formed

  - Lithium nitride is made when 1 nitride ion and 3 lithium ions form ionic bonds
- The final ionic solid of Li<sub>3</sub>N is **neutral** in charge:

![Chemical Bonding Lithium Nitride Cross Diagram, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes](assets/c76b8f922845-1-3-chemical-bonding-lithium-nitride-cross-diagr.png)

**Dot & cross aluminium oxide**

Draw a dot and cross diagram for aluminium oxide, Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>.

**Answer**

- Aluminium is a Group 3 **metal**

  - It **loses** its outer electrons to form an aluminium ion with a +3 charge (Al<sup>3+</sup>)
- Oxygen is a Group 6 **non-metal**

  - It **gains** 2 electrons to form an oxide ion with a -2 charge (O<sup>2-</sup>)
- To cancel out the negative and positive charges, 2 aluminium and 3 oxygen atoms are needed

  - Aluminium oxide is made when 2 aluminium ions and 3 oxygen ions form ionic bonds
- The final ionic solid of Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> is **neutral** in charge:

![Chemical Bonding Aluminium Oxide Cross Diagram, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes](assets/be60f4a16694-1-3-chemical-bonding-aluminium-oxide-cross-diagr.png)
